newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japanese prime minister scolds Nomura over scandal.
newsitem.headline: Japanese prime minister scolds Nomura over scandal.

text.p: Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto said on Thursday that a scandal involving Nomura Securities Co Ltd was "extremely regrettable" and called on the brokerage to reflect on its misdeeds.
Hashimoto also said that the finance minister would take strict measures against Nomura if the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission (SESC) recommended that it do so.
Hashimoto urged Nomura to reflect on the damage it had done to international confidence in Japan's securities industry.
"I cannot use any other words except 'extremely regrettable'," Hashimoto said.
"I understand that the SESC, which is an independent body, will take appropriate measures against actions which are specific violations (of the law)."
"I want Nomura to at least be aware again of the damage it has done to the confidence in (Japan's) securities industry in international society," Hashimoto said.
Hashimoto had to step down as finance minister in 1991 after Nomura and other Japanese brokerages were involved in a big industry scandal.

Asked about the Justice Ministry's view on the incident, an official from the ministry said that, in principle, prosecutors will take appropriate measures if there is evidence that it should be handled as a criminal case.
